children.text: Making more of the roof space

This Solihull design proposal explores the potential for additional accommodation within the roof of a familiar family house. A full-width rear dormer creates a broad garden-facing elevation and a more upright space at loft level, while retaining the garden below.
A modern finish with a simple form

Charcoal standing-seam metal cladding gives the dormer a clean, contemporary appearance above the original red brick. Two wide windows balance daylight with areas of solid wall. Slim frames and a restrained roof edge keep the detailing quiet, with a strip of existing roof tiles visible below.
Space shaped around everyday needs

The loft could be developed around a bedroom, a quiet workspace or flexible family accommodation. A measured survey would establish the available headroom and how a staircase could connect to the floor below before the internal layout is fixed.

children.text: Extra room above an established home

This Sutton Coldfield proposal considers how a conventional semi-detached house could accommodate changing family needs within its roof space. A broad rear dormer creates a starting point for extra accommodation while keeping the outdoor space available for everyday use.
Crisp detailing above a traditional house

Graphite standing-seam cladding introduces a modern material above the cream-rendered elevation. Two broad windows are separated by a solid panel, giving the dormer a calm, balanced face. A slim roof edge and retained tiled strip below connect the new form to the existing roof.
Starting with a useful layout

The next design stage would test the stair position, usable headroom, furniture and storage before assigning rooms. The window arrangement provides a starting point that can develop alongside the measured layout and the homeowner's priorities.

children.text: Looking upwards for additional space

This Stourbridge design proposal explores the roof of a traditional end-of-terrace house. The aim is to consider additional accommodation within the home while retaining the compact rear garden for sitting outside, planting and everyday family use.
A warmer take on a modern dormer

Bronze-toned standing-seam cladding complements the red brick while giving the dormer a clearly contemporary finish. Two dark-framed windows and a slim roof trim keep the broad rear elevation simple. A narrow strip of roof tiles remains below the dormer, and the adjoining terrace roof stays visually separate.
A room shaped around the existing house

The loft could be explored as a bedroom, workspace or another flexible room, depending on the measured roof and the homeowner's priorities. Stair access, headroom and the relationship with the existing first floor would guide the layout.
